key_insight: A PT-symmetric altermagnetic topological-insulator heterostructure can generate a pure spin bulk photovoltaic effect with zero charge photocurrent when symmetry forbids charge transport.
engineering_relevance: By tuning the Néel vector orientation, the device can switch between pure spin output and mixed charge-spin response, offering a symmetry-based route to controllable spin-photonic devices.
method: Built a 2D heterostructure combining a topological insulator with a d-wave altermagnet.
Developed a non-Abelian theory for spin BPVE in PT-degenerate band manifolds.
Analyzed how Néel-vector rotation changes topological phase and nonlinear optical response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports symmetry-resolved theoretical results showing vanishing second-order charge currents under C2z symmetry, while spin photocurrents remain finite and change sign with the local Dirac mass.
watch_item: The effect relies on precise symmetry conditions and magnetic orientation control, so experimental disorder, symmetry breaking, or imperfect Néel-vector alignment could reduce the pure-spin response.
paper_title: Pure Spin Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in an Altermagnetic Higher-Order Topological Insulator
